dedupe_keys.name: infrastructure protection and population response to infrastructure failure uk us japan germany new zealand

description: This UK Data Service collection holds the qualitative material from an ESRC-funded comparative project (grant ES/K000233/1) on how governments prepare citizens for the collapse of critical national infrastructure, how they model collapse and population response, and how infrastructure protection policy has changed over time. It covers the UK, the United States, Japan, Germany and New Zealand, chosen to represent different welfare regimes, with a time period from 1945 to 2015. The methods were archival research in national archives on planned and actual population response to disasters, focus groups and interviews with selected experts, and case studies of actual infrastructure failures prepared as summary notes from documentary evidence, with particular reference to health and education. It was produced by John Preston and Charlotte Chadderton at the University of East London, with data collection from 2012 to 2015, and deposited in December 2015. The UK Data Service states the collection is available to any user without registration for download, as text files. Caveats: the material is qualitative and policy-focused, it holds no quantitative model of population behaviour, and the country selection is limited to developed economies. It is useful for grounding emergency response and agent-based models of public behaviour during infrastructure failure, and for cascading failure and resilience scenario design; a related record is the Medellín cascading effects community datasets.
